# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

Create `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — audio capture and silence detection.

**Responsibilities:**
- Spawn the configurable capture command (default: arecord -f S16_LE -r 16000 -c 1) as a child process
- Read raw 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM from stdout in fixed-size frames (e.g. 160 bytes = 10 ms)
- Compute per-frame RMS energy for silence/pause detection
- Emit data events with PCM frame buffers + RMS value
- Track silence: emit silence event after configurable idle duration (default 3 s)
- Track pause: emit pause event when silence exceeds a longer threshold (e.g. 2 s) for partial transcription triggers
- Handle capture process exit: emit error with actionable message
- Graceful shutdown: send SIGINT to capture process on stop

**Key APIs:**
- child_process.spawn() for capture command
- Node.js Readable stream for PCM framing
- RMS computation on 16-bit PCM samples

**Unit tests (TDD — no real microphone; feed synthetic PCM):**
- RMS computation over known 16-bit sample buffers
- Silence fires after exactly the configured idle duration (deterministic clock)
- Speech keeps the silence timer reset; mixed speech/silence sequences
- Pause event cadence for partial transcription
- Capture process exit surfaces an actionable error, never throws
data.title: Recorder module: capture process, PCM framing, silence detection

Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client
data.title: Whisper worker protocol: persistent Python worker and TypeScript client

## Summary

The audit runner's Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest omits the audited item's **committed** touched files whenever the working tree is clean, causing false "outside the manifest" / `unmet` verdicts for criteria whose implementation and tests live in those committed files.

Discovered during the audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (log: `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T095408.log`).

## Evidence

- The audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX returned `Ready to close: No` with parent AC1 `partial`, AC2 `unmet`, AC3 `unmet` — each justified by wording such as "`test_cache._default_runner`/`run_tests.py` are outside the provided manifest" and "test_cache is outside the manifest so its runner cannot be verified".
- The item's implementation commit `a83ada6a` changed 14 files (`git show --stat a83ada6a`): `.githooks/pre-push`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`, `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`.
- `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --name-only` returns all of those files, so the data is available — the manifest simply did not use it.
- The manifest actually used contained only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`; the latter is **not** in `a83ada6a`.
- The working tree was clean at audit time (`git status --porcelain` showed only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

## Root cause

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4351`) builds the manifest's file list from:

1. the description's Key Files (`_extract_key_files`);
2. `_git_changed_files()` (`audit_runner.py:4210`) — `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain=v1`, i.e. **working-tree / untracked changes only**;
3. Phase 1 evidence `file:line` refs;
4. a lightweight repo index.

It does **not** use `_resolve_touched_files()` (`audit_runner.py:1476`), which already resolves the union of (a) files in commits referencing the item id (`git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only`), (b) comment-recorded commit hashes, and (c) Key Files — the correct source for a fully-committed item on a clean checkout.

Consequently, when an item's work is committed and the tree is clean (the normal post-implementation state), `_git_changed_files()` contributes nothing and the manifest collapses to the Phase 1 evidence refs + repo index. The `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` fail-fast guard (`audit_runner.py:1231`) does not abort because the manifest does reference *some* item-repo file, even though it omits the item's actual touched files.

## Desired behaviour

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` must include the audited item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`), so a clean checkout still yields a manifest covering the item's real changes. The fail-fast scope validation must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the audited item's committed touched files (reuse `_resolve_touched_files()`), in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Regression test: with a clean working tree and a committed commit whose message references the item id, the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts that a manifest which references the item repo but omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is impossible to build).
- [ ] Re-auditing SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX after this fix no longer reports its ACs as "outside the manifest" solely because the item's files are committed rather than uncommitted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_validate_file_scope_manifest`
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — the audit whose false-negative verdicts surfaced this defect.
- Blocks the accurate re-audit/closure of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (dependency edge recorded).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (RESOLVED) — Does AC3 require hardening `_validate_file_scope_manifest()`, or is the "impossible to build" regression test sufficient? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** AC3 says a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files must be "rejected (or is impossible to build)". The Desired-behaviour section separately states the fail-fast scope validation "must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files", which reads as a validator-hardening requirement.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** harden `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` with an optional `touched_files` argument: when a non-empty touched set is resolvable and none of its paths appear in the manifest, return a scope error; when the set is `None`/empty, fail open (preserves current behaviour for mono-repo/unknown cases). Plan child SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O covers this; the regression test is delivered either way.
- **Alternative A:** satisfy AC3 solely with the "impossible to build" regression test (no validator change).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **harden**. `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` gains an optional `touched_files` argument that returns a scope error when a non-empty resolved touched set has no path in the manifest, and fails open when the set is `None`/empty. Delivered by SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O; the regression test is still required.

### Q2 (RESOLVED) — The item's `effort`/`risk` fields are lowercase ("medium"/"medium"), so the plan-approval gate's documented Medium-effort trigger did not fire. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `should_request_plan_approval()` compares `effort` case-sensitively against `{"Medium", "Large", "Extra Large"}`. `wl show` reports this item's values as `"medium"`/`"medium"` (other items, e.g. SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX, use `"Medium"`/`"Severe"`). `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` therefore returned `request_approval: false`, skipping the human checkpoint the skill documents for Medium effort.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** correct the item's `effort`/`risk` to canonical capitalised values and, if plan sign-off is wanted, review the child breakdown before implementation. (Making the gate case-insensitive is a separate change, out of scope here.)
- **Alternative A:** accept the gate result as-is and proceed without a producer approval pause (what this run did).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **correct**. The item's `effort`/`risk` were set to the canonical capitalised values (`Medium`/`Medium`) via `wl update`. With the corrected data, `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` ("its effort is Medium scale"), so the plan is surfaced to the producer for sign-off before implementation.

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` only exits the AC section on an `##` heading, so an H1-headed description makes the AC-coverage review treat Key Files / Related-work bullets as ACs and recommend `stop`. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` detects the AC header with `^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria` but breaks only on `^##\s+`. This plan normalised this item's and its children's headings to `##` (conformant with the AGENTS.md `## Acceptance Criteria` convention) so coverage parses correctly. Tracked as discovered-from work item SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** reaffirm the H2 convention for descriptions and make the extractor break on any heading level 1–6 for robustness.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — informational; no plan decision depends on it._

### Plan approval (2026-09-27)

- **Decision:** APPROVED — producer replied "LGTM" to the four-child, test-first plan (SA-0MUKCOQI10095463 → SA-0MUKCOUXN001VH47 → SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O → SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6). The plan-approval gate (Medium effort) is satisfied; `needsProducerReview` is cleared and the plan is ready for implementation.
data.title: Audit FILE SCOPE manifest omits a clean tree's committed touched files, causing false out-of-scope verdicts

# Summary

The audit skill (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) references a `.ralph.json` / `ralph.config.json` config system that no longer exists in this repository. Ralph is not present anywhere on disk (no `skill/ralph` directory, no config files, no project references). These references are dead code and stale documentation.

## Dead code in `audit_runner.py`

- `ASSET_CONFIG_PATH` — points to `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` (missing).
- `RALPH_CONFIG_FILES` — references `.ralph.json` and `ralph.config.json` (neither exists).
- `_load_asset_config()` — loads from missing asset path (fails open to `{}`).
- `_load_config()` — merges asset defaults with CWD config files.
- `_deep_merge()` — helper for `_load_config()`.
- `_extract_phase_model_config()` — extracts per-phase model config from loaded JSON.
- `_resolve_model_for_phase()` — resolves model from config with multi-source resolution.
- `_resolve_phase1_model()` — resolves Phase 1 model (fast/cheap) vs Phase 2 (full).
- `_resolve_phase_model_value()` — resolves a model string from nested config.
- `_coerce_model_str()` — coerces model string.
- `_model_source()` — resolves model source (local/remote).
- CLI flags `--model` and `--phase1-model` — allow overriding the model via config file resolution.
- Docstrings and help text referencing `.ralph.json` / `ralph.config.json`.

# Discord release report: add project elevator pitch and per-release focus paragraphs

## Problem statement

The Discord release notification currently opens with the itemised changelog, which assumes the reader already knows what the project/game is and what this release is about. Channel readers without prior context cannot tell what the project does or what the headline change of the release is without reading the whole changelog.

## Users

- **Release operators / producers** who post release announcements to a shared Discord channel and want the announcement to be self-explanatory.
- **Players / stakeholders / channel readers** who see the announcement and need immediate context.

User stories:

- As a channel reader, I want a 2–3 sentence elevator pitch of the project/game first, so I can understand the announcement without prior context.
- As a release operator, I want a 1–3 sentence summary of the release's main focus, so the headline change is obvious before the itemised changelog.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Ordering and content.** The Discord release embed description is composed of paragraphs in this order: (a) the project elevator pitch (2–3 sentences), (b) the release focus summary (1–3 sentences), (c) the existing project/version line, (d) the changelog section. Verified by unit tests asserting the built payload's paragraph order and content.
- **Pitch sourcing.** The pitch is read from a new `projectDescription` field resolved with the same three-layer precedence as `projectName` (`.worklog/config.private.yaml` → `.worklog/config.yaml` → `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`). When unset, a pitch is generated via the existing DeepSeek LLM pattern from the leading prose of `README.md` (the block before the first `##` heading, capped at ~1000 characters); when generation is unavailable (no API key, LLM error, or missing/unreadable README) the pitch paragraph is omitted. Verified by unit tests with injected config paths and a faked LLM boundary.
- **Focus generation and extraction.** `generate-changelog.js` generates the release focus from the release's work items in its existing LLM pass and persists it in the new `CHANGELOG.md` version section as a machine-extractable marker line (`> **Release focus:** …`) directly under the version heading. `discord-notify.js` extracts that marker, produces the focus paragraph, and removes the marker from the changelog body sent to Discord so the text is not duplicated. When no marker exists, the paragraph is omitted and the changelog renders unchanged.
- **Non-blocking contract preserved.** Every new failure path (missing config, missing API key, LLM error, missing README, missing focus marker) logs an info/warning line and returns without changing the release exit code; the existing behaviours (webhook precedence, skip when unset, HTTP/network failure warning) are unchanged, and the composed description is still truncated to ≤ 4096 characters.
- **Test coverage.** Unit tests cover: pitch from config, pitch from README/LLM fallback, pitch omitted, focus marker generation in the changelog section, focus extraction and de-duplication from the changelog body, focus omitted, paragraph ordering, truncation of the composed description, and config precedence. All LLM/network boundaries are injected (no live network, no live home config or worklog mutation).
- **Documentation and suite.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (`skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`), including the `projectDescription` config schema entry and fallback semantics. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependencies** — Node.js 18+ built-ins only (`fetch`, `AbortSignal`), consistent with `discord-notify.js` today.
- **LLM access** uses the existing `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` + DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the graceful `null` fallback. The shared caller is extracted into a small `llm.js` module; `discord-notify.js` must **not** import `generate-changelog.js` (it runs `git rev-parse` at module import).
- **No tracked-file mutation at release time** — the README-derived pitch is generated on the fly and not persisted to `.worklog/config.yaml`, avoiding a dirty worktree mid-release (which could interfere with the post-merge dev sync). Documented assumption; persistence can be a follow-up.
- **English:** all docs/comments must use UK English.
- **Existing notification behaviour** (webhook precedence, skip when unset, HTTP failure non-blocking) must be unchanged.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` builds the embed: title `<projectName> Release v<version>`, description `**<projectName> v<version>**` + changelog section, fields Version / Tag / Date / PR. It has a minimal YAML subset parser supporting top-level scalars and one level of nesting.
- `projectName` is resolved from `.worklog/config.private.yaml` → `.worklog/config.yaml` → `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD).
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` runs a per-work-item LLM pass (`callLlm`, DeepSeek, `null` fallback) and `generateReleaseSection()` emits `## vX.Y.Z (date)` followed by `### Features` / `### Bug Fixes` / `### Other`.
- `run-release.js` calls `sendReleaseNotification({version, prUrl, projectRoot})` after merge verification, never on `--dry-run`.

## Desired change

- New config field `projectDescription` (top-level scalar in `.worklog/config.yaml`) resolved with the same precedence chain as `projectName`; documented in the ship reference and example config.
- New shared module `skill/ship/scripts/llm.js` exporting `callLlm(messages, opts)` (moved from `generate-changelog.js`, which imports it from there).
- `generate-changelog.js`: request a 1–3 sentence focus paragraph from the LLM over the release's categorised items and persist it as `> **Release focus:** …` directly under the version heading; omit when the LLM is unavailable.
- `discord-notify.js`: extract the `> **Release focus:**` marker (and remove it from the changelog body); resolve the pitch (`projectDescription`, else README/LLM, else omit); compose the description as pitch → focus → project/version line → changelog; truncate the composed description at 4096 characters.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — pitch resolution (+ README/LLM fallback), focus extraction, new description order; keep existing config helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — release-focus generation and section marker.
- `skill/ship/scripts/llm.js` — new shared LLM caller (extracted; graceful `null` fallback).
- `tests/unit/test-discord-notify.mjs` — ordering / fallback / extraction tests.
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-query.mjs` (or a new `test-generate-changelog-focus.mjs`) — focus marker generation tests.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — mirrored coverage.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — documentation.
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — optional `projectDescription` example/pitch for this repository.

## Related work

- **Ship skill: send Discord message with release details + changelog on successful release (SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z)** — the notification feature this extends; its non-blocking/truncation contracts carry over.
- **Ship report to discord needs titling (SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD)** — introduced `projectName` resolution; the closest precedent for `projectDescription`.
- **Move release-notification (Discord) webhook secret into a gitignored per-project `.worklog/config.private.yaml` (SA-0MUF833QL001WJXD)** — established the config precedence chain.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "create it with LLM from the start of the README" means generate the pitch at release time, not persist it. Rationale: persisting would dirty the tracked worktree during the release pipeline (risking the post-merge `dev` sync). *Producer action: confirm; if persistence is wanted, raise a follow-up work item.*
- **Assumption:** "the start of the README" means the leading prose block before the first `##` heading; when the README is missing or has no prose, generation is skipped and the pitch omitted.
- **Risk:** LLM-generated focus/pitch may be bland or misleading. Mitigation: bounded length (pitch 2–3 sentences, focus 1–3), focus persisted in `CHANGELOG.md` for review, omission on failure, and config text always wins over generation.
- **Risk:** extra LLM latency/cost in the release path. Mitigation: one focus call per release (piggybacking the existing changelog LLM pass) plus at most one pitch call; bounded 30 s timeout; non-blocking.
- **Risk:** truncation could cut the pitch/focus paragraphs. Mitigation: prompt-enforced brevity; existing 4096-char truncation retained.
- **Risk (scope creep):** extending generation to all projects' configs. Mitigation: feature is config-driven/opt-in; only the fallback generator is universal. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Source of the project elevator pitch?" — Answer (operator): "A (if not present then create it with LLM from the start of the README)". Source: interactive reply. Implication: `projectDescription` config field with README/LLM fallback; omission when generation unavailable.
- Q2: "Source of the per-release focus paragraph?" — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply. Implication: LLM-generated during the existing `generate-changelog.js` pass, persisted in the `CHANGELOG.md` version section, extracted by `discord-notify.js`.
- Q3: "Behaviour when a pitch/focus paragraph is unavailable?" — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply. Implication: omit the paragraph silently; preserve the non-blocking release semantics and the existing notification content.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPDZEDED005YYIJ** – Docs: Update agent/ship.md & release docs (completed)
- **SA-0MQ1O0XIQ00345VM** – Include pi command and work item title in Ralph event/Discord notifications (completed)
- **SA-0MLK57HG10JDXRJA** – Docs for implement preflight + new skill (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, first, followed, high, initial (+15 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: add, first, focus, followed, high (+14 more)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — matched: add, first, focus, followed, high (+13 more)

## Plan: changelog

| Date (UTC) | Action | Details |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-05 | Plan created | Decomposed into 4 child items (1 refactor + 2 features + 1 docs). Key Files header fixed (`## **Key Files:**` → `**Key Files:**`). Dependencies mapped. Vertical slice phasing applied. |

- Q4: "Should the plan be approved?" — Decision: approval not required (effort Small, risk Medium — below plan-approval gate threshold). Proceeded to implementation planning.

- Q5: "Pitch persistence into config?" — Assumption (documented): pitch is generated on the fly, not persisted. Rationale: persisting would dirty the tracked worktree during release. Producer action: confirmed by operator in intake (Q1). If persistence is wanted, raise as a follow-up work item.

## Summary

The audit runner cannot re-audit an item in the terminal `completed`/`done` state: its entry status lifecycle unconditionally claims the item with `wl update <id> --status in_progress` (no `--stage`), and the worklog rejects `in-progress`/`done` as an incompatible status/stage pair.

## Evidence

Reproduced from a clean checkout against a scratch item:

```text
$ wl update <done-item> --status in_progress --json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Invalid status/stage combination: status \"in-progress\" is not compatible with stage \"done\". Allowed stages for status \"in-progress\": intake_complete, plan_complete. Allowed statuses for stage \"done\": completed, deleted."
}
```

The ContextHub compatibility guard (`isStatusStageCompatible`) only whitelists the audit-runner transitional pair for `in-progress` with `in_review`, `idea`, `intake_complete`, and `plan_complete` — not `done`.

This blocks parent SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M AC4: re-auditing the already-`done` SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (child SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6, which forbids reopening the item).

## Desired behaviour

Re-auditing a `completed`/`done` item must work without reopening it. A `done` item is already terminal, so the runner must not attempt the invalid `in-progress`/`done` claim; it should run the audit and let the verdict-driven terminal lifecycle keep/restore `done` (Yes), demote to `open`/`plan_complete` (No), or restore `completed`/`done` (failure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cmd_issue` does not issue an invalid `--status in_progress` claim for a `completed`/`done` item.
- [ ] Regression test: auditing a `completed`/`done` item with a `Ready to close: Yes` report completes without the invalid claim and leaves the item `completed`/`done`.
- [ ] Regression test: a `Ready to close: No` re-audit of a `done` item demotes it to `open`/`plan_complete`.
- [ ] Regression test: an infra failure on a `done` item restores `completed`/`done`.
- [ ] Existing lifecycle tests remain green; full suite green.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`cmd_issue` entry claim, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocks SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6 (re-audit SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX).
- discovered-from:SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M.
